summary.intent: Recover uncommitted Phase 37 (parallel batch upload pipeline) planning work from a previous session, gather implementation decisions via the GSD discuss workflow, and kick off research + planning for the phase.
summary.outcome: Phase 37 CONTEXT.md and DISCUSSION-LOG.md were created and committed with all key implementation decisions locked. The plan-phase workflow was initiated and a researcher agent was spawned. A parallel worktree was also created off main for concurrent work.

repo: The current upload pipeline in useDropUpload.ts:113-133 loops sequentially — each file calls client.uploadFile() which does encrypt → IPFS pin → add FilePointer → publish folder IPNS, resulting in N IPNS publishes for N files.

The SDK's withOperation() serializes all SDK operations, meaning concurrent calls to uploadFile() would just queue and remain sequential — Option C (batching at web layer with existing API) is not viable.

The desktop FUSE layer receives files one-at-a-time via filesystem release() callbacks and has no batch context, so a Rust upload_files() batch method would not be used by the FUSE layer without a separate write-coalescing architecture.
Phase 36 (inline upload progress) already established per-file Zustand store tracking with cancel, retry, and error states — Phase 37 builds on this foundation.

The stale-children race window is a known risk for batch uploads: concurrent publishes on the same folder can silently drop files if folder.children is read at start and published after a long encrypt+pin window.

code.finding: Sequential file upload loop — each iteration calls client.uploadFile() triggering encrypt+pin+IPNS publish per file.
uploadFile() is one atomic unit: encrypt+pin+publish. Breaking it apart requires a new batch method rather than composing existing calls.
FUSE release() callback triggers per-file upload — no batch context available at this layer.
Rust SDK uses a queue for upload operations — write-coalescing would need to be added here or above this layer.

workflow: GSD discuss-phase workflow was run in 'discuss' mode (not 'assumptions' mode) — the mode is configured via gsd-tools config-get workflow.discuss_mode.
Uncommitted planning artifacts (ROADMAP.md edits, empty phase directories) from a previous session were still present as local working tree changes and were recoverable.
The GSD init tool (gsd-tools.cjs init phase-op) provides has_context, has_plans, phase_dir, etc. flags that drive workflow branching decisions.
A parallel git worktree can be created off main for concurrent work alongside an active feature branch.

friction: Phase 37 roadmap entry and phase directory were never committed in the previous session, causing confusion about whether the work was merged to main.

The SDK's withOperation() serialization was a hidden constraint that made the seemingly simple 'run uploadFile() concurrently' approach completely unviable — this wasn't obvious without reading the SDK internals.
The error/partial-failure discussion loop was redundant — a question was asked whose answer had already been established, requiring clarification mid-discussion.
open_items: Adaptive concurrency based on file size (deferred — start with fixed pool of 3).
FUSE write-coalescing for desktop batch publish optimization — separate phase needed.
Accumulated retry batching — deferred until failure patterns are observed in production.
Rust SDK upload_files() for API parity — noted but not in scope for this phase.
Stale-children race window mitigation (re-read folder metadata just before final publish) — needs to be addressed in implementation.
Memory spike prevention during parallel encryption — pipeline-style processing (encrypt→pin→free per slot) rather than encrypt-all-then-pin-all.
Plan-phase researcher agent was spawned but transcript ends before research or planning completes — Phase 37 planning is still in progress.
